claims.statement: The proposed extension incorporates representations of relative positions, or distances between sequence elements, directly into Transformer self-attention.
The authors claim an efficient implementation of self-attention with relative position representations.
The proposed relative position representations are invariant to total sequence length.

The relative position mechanism can be cast as a special case of self-attention extended to represent arbitrary relations between any two input elements; applying this framework to labeled, directed graphs is proposed as future work.
On WMT 2014 English-to-German translation, the approach yields a reported improvement of 1.3 BLEU over absolute position representations.
On WMT 2014 English-to-French translation, the approach yields a reported improvement of 0.3 BLEU over absolute position representations.
Combining relative and absolute position representations yields no further improvement in translation quality in the reported experiments.
Relative position representations improve translation quality on both reported machine translation tasks even when they entirely replace absolute position encodings.
For linear sequences, edge labels encode relative-position differences clipped to a maximum absolute distance k, producing 2k + 1 unique edge labels.
The authors claim that clipping relative distances enables generalization to sequence lengths not seen during training.
Separate learned key and value relative-position representations are indexed by clip(j − i, k), where clip(x, k) = max(−k, min(k, x)).
Simple addition incorporates edge representations into both output and compatibility computations, primarily to enable efficient implementation.
The extension represents pairwise relationships between input elements as a labeled, directed, fully connected graph.

Each edge has two distinct learned representations for use in output and compatibility computations without additional linear transformations; these representations can be shared across attention heads, and the authors use da = dz.
The extension propagates edge information to the sublayer output and accounts for edges when determining attention compatibility.
The output computation is zi = sum_j αij(xj WV + aV_ij).
The compatibility computation is eij = (xi WQ)(xj WK + aK_ij)^T / sqrt(dz).

Sharing relative-position representations across attention heads reduces their storage complexity from O(h n² d_a) to O(n² d_a); sharing across sequences gives overall self-attention space complexity O(b h n d_z + n² d_a), compared with O(b h n d_z) without these representations.
Splitting attention compatibility computation into an ordinary attention term and a relative-position term permits efficient computation while avoiding broadcasting relative-position representations.

Tensor reshaping computes the relative-position compatibility term using n parallel multiplications of bh × d_z and d_z × n matrices; further reshaping allows addition to the ordinary term, and the same approach applies to the attention output computation.
In the reported machine translation experiments, the implementation decreased steps per second by 7% while maintaining the model and batch sizes used by Vaswani et al. (2017) on P100 GPUs.
In base-model experiments without absolute position representations, BLEU on the WMT English-to-German newstest2013 development set varied little for tested relative-distance clipping values k ≥ 2.

The translation comparison replaces sinusoidal position encodings with relative-position representations and uses regenerated Transformer baseline results to isolate the effect from other library and experimental-configuration changes.

On the WMT 2014 translation tasks evaluated using newstest2014, relative positions improved English-to-German BLEU by 0.3 for the base configuration and 1.3 for the big configuration, and English-to-French BLEU by 0.5 and 0.3, respectively.

The unverified Table 1 extraction reports base-model BLEU scores of 26.5 and 38.2 with absolute positions versus 26.8 and 38.7 with relative positions, for English-to-German and English-to-French respectively.

The unverified Table 1 extraction reports big-model BLEU scores of 27.9 and 41.2 with absolute positions versus 29.2 and 41.5 with relative positions, for English-to-German and English-to-French respectively.
The authors evaluated separate ablations of the two relative position representations, aV_ij in equation (3) and aK_ij in equation (4).
The unverified Table 2 extraction reports EN-DE BLEU scores of 12.5, 25.5, 25.8, 25.9, 25.8, 25.9, and 25.8 for clipping distances k = 0, 1, 2, 4, 16, 64, and 256, respectively.
The unverified Table 3 extraction reports EN-DE BLEU of 25.8 with both representations, 25.8 with only aK_ij, 25.3 with only aV_ij, and 12.5 with neither representation.
The authors suggest that including relative position representations only when determining compatibility between elements may be sufficient, while leaving applicability to other tasks unresolved.
The authors report that their relative-position self-attention extension improves machine translation performance.
